entry.title: It's easy to get addicted to the dopamine loop of Jira tickets moving to 'Done
entry.summary:
It's easy to get addicted to the dopamine loop of Jira tickets moving to 'Done'. You ship feature after feature, close ticket after ticket, and rack up sprint points. But if your health is degrading, your friendships are fading, and you haven't taken a walk in daylight for a week, what are you actually winning? The sprint board never empties. There will always be another ticket waiting for you. Ship your work, but make sure you have a real life waiting when you shut the lid. Build a life, not just a backlog.

entry.title: Our sign-in codes went to Junk, and every check passed
entry.summary: Stagd signs people in with a code by email. People who review previews, such as designers, product managers and clients, often have no GitHub account, so the code is how they get in. It has one job: arrive within a minute, in the inbox. At a Gmail address it did. At a Microsoft 365 address it went to Junk, or didn't show up at all. This is how we found out why, and why the usual checklist wasn't the answer. When mail goes to spam, the first suspects are always the same three records, so we checked them first: SPF: passed, through the bounce domain our sending service uses. DKIM: passed, signed for our own domain. DMARC: passed, with a p=reject policy, the strictest there is. Microsoft agreed. The headers of a junked code said so in its own words: spf=pass dkim=pass header.d=stagd-staging.…

entry.title: The car on your ride-hailing map is a guess
entry.summary: The car on a ride-hailing map is not where the driver is. It is where the app guesses the driver is. The driver's phone reports a GPS position every few seconds, not continuously. If the rider's app drew each report the moment it arrived, the car would teleport from point to point. So the app animates the car from one report toward the next, and the animation is invented. Most of the time the invention is good. Sometimes the car takes a strange turn, cuts through a building and snaps back to the road. The guess was off, and the next real position corrected it. I don't know how Uber, Careem or any other app implements this, and each one tunes its own details. This article describes the general pattern and one way to build it in Kotlin with Flow, including the numbers you have to choose and …

entry.title: Your sitemap lastmod Is Lying. Here's a 40-Line Fix That Made Mine Honest
entry.summary: If your site is built from templates, there is a good chance every page in your sitemap has the same lastmod date — the date of your last deploy. That is not a lie you tell on purpose. It falls out of the build: a footer change touches all 1,287 files, the generator stamps each one with now(), and the sitemap faithfully reports that the entire site changed at 14:32 on Tuesday. To a crawler, that means: nothing here is more important than anything else. So it re-checks everything, in whatever order it feels like, and the pages you actually care about wait in the same queue as the ones nobody will ever link to. I had exactly this. entry.title: How to Reduce Wind Noise in an Outdoor Interview Recording
entry.summary: An outdoor interview can contain traffic, footsteps and wind on the microphone at the same time. The useful question is not whether every pause can become silent. It is whether the conversation becomes easier to understand without changing the words or making the voice unstable. Keep the original recording and edit a copy. Note where the important answers occur before processing. One setting may work for a calm passage but damage a quieter answer recorded just after a gust. Steady hiss and distant environmental noise differ from bursts of air striking a microphone. Wind may create very low-frequency energy or overload the recording. Speech denoising can reduce some unwanted sound, but is not a reliable repair for clipped audio or missing syllables. Listen to the speaker's softest words as …
